protocols.title: Chest Pain - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
CHEST PAIN (Cardiac-type pain, Central chest pain, Crushing pain)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise
- Inadequate breathing
- Shock (cold, clammy, HR>100, SBP<90)
- Unresponsive or only responds to pain
- Ongoing cardiac arrest

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Severe pain (8-10/10)
- Cardiac pain: crushing, tight, radiating to arm/jaw/back
- Abnormal pulse (irregular, very fast >120, very slow <50)
- New neurological deficit
- Significant cardiac history with new symptoms
- Hypotension (SBP <100)
- Acutely short of breath

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Moderate pain (4-7/10)
- Pleuritic pain (sharp, worse on breathing)
- Cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, smoking, family history)
- History of cardiac disease with similar previous pain
- Age >35 with new chest pain
- Associated symptoms: nausea, sweating, palpitations

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Mild pain (<4/10)
- Musculoskeletal chest pain (reproducible on palpation)
- Recent minor illness (cold/cough) with chest discomfort
- Anxiety-related chest tightness
- Known non-cardiac cause

Key Discriminators:
- Cardiac pain, Pleuritic pain, Severity of pain
- Abnormal pulse, Signs of shock, Hypotension
- Associated shortness of breath, Diaphoresis

Immediate Actions:
- ECG within 10 minutes for Orange/Red
- Continuous monitoring for Red/Orange
- IV access, Aspirin if cardiac suspected

protocols.title: Shortness of Breath - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
SHORTNESS OF BREATH (Difficulty breathing, Breathlessness, Respiratory distress)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise (stridor, drooling, unable to swallow)
- Inadequate breathing (apnoea, gasping, exhaustion)
- Shock
- Unresponsive or responds to pain only
- Very low SpO2 (<85% on air)
- Cannot speak in sentences

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Severe respiratory distress (accessory muscle use, tripod position)
- SpO2 <92% on air
- Unable to speak in full sentences
- Stridor or severe wheeze
- Altered conscious level
- Exhaustion from breathing effort
- Acute onset severe breathlessness
- Anaphylaxis features (rash + breathing difficulty)

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Moderate respiratory distress
- SpO2 92-94% on air
- New wheeze or increased wheeze
- Increased work of breathing
- Known asthma/COPD with worsening symptoms
- Fever with respiratory symptoms
- Unable to complete sentences comfortably

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Mild breathlessness on exertion only
- SpO2 >95% on air
- Normal respiratory rate and effort
- Chronic stable symptoms
- Recent mild illness with slight breathlessness

Key Discriminators:
- SpO2 level, Respiratory rate, Work of breathing
- Ability to speak in sentences
- Stridor, Wheeze, Signs of exhaustion
- Associated features (fever, rash, cough)

Immediate Actions:
- Oxygen therapy if SpO2 <94%
- Sitting upright position
- Nebulisers if wheeze/bronchospasm
- Peak flow if asthma

protocols.title: Headache - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
HEADACHE (Head pain, Migraine, Severe headache)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise
- Inadequate breathing
- Shock
- Unresponsive or responds to pain only
- Currently fitting
- Signs of meningococcal septicaemia (purpuric rash)

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Sudden onset severe headache (thunderclap - worst ever, peak within seconds)
- Altered conscious level (drowsy, confused)
- New focal neurological deficit (weakness, speech problems, visual loss)
- Signs of meningism (neck stiffness, photophobia, Kernig's positive)
- Non-blanching rash with fever
- Very high temperature (>40°C)
- Severe pain (8-10/10)
- Recent significant head injury with new headache

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Moderate to severe pain (4-7/10)
- First severe headache or different from usual
- Headache with fever
- Headache with vomiting
- Headache with visual disturbance
- Age >50 with new type headache
- Known raised intracranial pressure
- Immunocompromised with headache and fever

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Mild headache (<4/10)
- Known migraine with typical features
- Tension-type headache
- Recent mild viral illness
- Headache responding to simple analgesia

Key Discriminators:
- Sudden onset, Severity, Thunderclap quality
- Signs of meningism, Fever, Rash
- Neurological deficit, Altered consciousness
- History of recent trauma

Immediate Actions:
- Urgent CT head if thunderclap headache
- LP if meningitis suspected (after CT)
- Neurological observations
- Analgesia and antiemetics

protocols.title: Abdominal Pain - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
ABDOMINAL PAIN (Stomach pain, Belly pain, Gastric pain)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise
- Inadequate breathing
- Shock (cold, clammy, tachycardia, hypotension)
- Unresponsive or responds to pain only
- Massive haematemesis or rectal bleeding
- Rigid abdomen with severe pain

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Severe pain (8-10/10)
- Signs of peritonism (guarding, rigidity, rebound)
- Haematemesis or melaena (fresh or altered blood)
- Absent bowel sounds with distension
- Severe vomiting with dehydration signs
- Signs of ectopic pregnancy (female of childbearing age with abdominal pain and PV bleeding)
- Known AAA with abdominal or back pain
- Significant abdominal trauma

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Moderate pain (4-7/10)
- Localised tenderness (RIF, RUQ, LIF)
- Vomiting without ability to tolerate fluids
- No passage of stool/flatus >24 hours
- Fever with abdominal pain
- Pregnancy with abdominal pain
- Testicular pain (male)
- Urinary symptoms with loin pain

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Mild pain (<4/10)
- Soft non-tender abdomen
- Normal bowel function
- No vomiting or mild self-limiting vomiting
- Recent dietary indiscretion
- Known IBS with typical symptoms

Key Discriminators:
- Severity of pain, Peritonism, Rigidity
- GI bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, fresh blood)
- Obstruction signs, Dehydration
- Pregnancy status in females

Immediate Actions:
- IV access and bloods for Orange/Red
- Pregnancy test in females of childbearing age
- Nil by mouth if surgical abdomen
- Analgesia (do not delay for surgical assessment)

protocols.title: Unwell Adult with Fever - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
UNWELL ADULT / FEVER (Generally unwell, Pyrexia, High temperature, Infection)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise
- Inadequate breathing
- Shock (cold peripheries, mottled, capillary refill >4s, hypotension)
- Unresponsive or responds to pain only
- Purpuric/non-blanching rash with fever (meningococcal sepsis)

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Very hot adult (temp >40°C / >104°F)
- Rigors or uncontrollable shaking
- Non-blanching rash
- Signs of severe sepsis (tachycardia >100, tachypnoea >25, confusion)
- Immunocompromised patient (chemo, steroids, HIV, splenectomy)
- Acutely confused or drowsy
- Purpura or petechiae with fever
- Unable to stand or walk
- Severe pain

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Hot adult (temp 38-40°C / 100-104°F)
- Localising signs of infection (cough, dysuria, cellulitis)
- Known infection not responding to antibiotics
- Return from malaria-endemic area with fever
- Persistent vomiting
- Moderate pain
- Recent surgery or invasive procedure

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Warm (temp <38°C / <100°F)
- No localising signs
- Self-caring and mobile
- Tolerating oral fluids
- Recent mild viral illness
- Low-grade temperature only

Key Discriminators:
- Temperature, Signs of sepsis/shock
- Non-blanching rash, Purpura
- Immunocompromise status
- Travel history, Localising symptoms

Immediate Actions:
- Sepsis 6 pathway if sepsis suspected
- Blood cultures before antibiotics
- IV access and fluids if shocked
- Malaria screen if travel history

protocols.title: Major Trauma - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
MAJOR TRAUMA (Injury, Accident, Fall, RTC)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise (stridor, unable to speak, facial burns)
- Inadequate breathing
- Shock (trauma with signs of haemorrhage)
- Unresponsive or responds to pain only (GCS <9)
- Exsanguinating haemorrhage
- Traumatic amputation (major limb)
- Penetrating injury to chest/abdomen/neck

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Significant mechanism (high speed RTC, fall >3m, ejection from vehicle)
- GCS 9-14 or any LOC
- Open or depressed skull fracture
- Suspected spinal injury with neurological symptoms
- Multiple long bone fractures
- Crush injury >15 minutes
- Burns >15% BSA adult (or airway concern)
- Penetrating limb injury with neurovascular compromise
- Severe pain
- Significant blood loss (visible or suspected)

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Moderate mechanism of injury
- Single long bone fracture or dislocation
- Head injury with brief or no LOC, now GCS 15
- Burns 5-15% BSA (not involving face/airway)
- Lacerations requiring suturing
- Moderate pain
- Unable to weight bear
- Spinal tenderness without neurological deficit

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Minor mechanism
- Small burns (<5% BSA, superficial)
- Minor soft tissue injury
- Mild pain
- Walking wounded with minor injury
- Simple wounds/abrasions

Key Discriminators:
- Mechanism of injury, GCS/consciousness
- Airway, Breathing, Circulation status
- Obvious fractures, Neurovascular compromise
- Burns extent and location

Immediate Actions:
- C-spine immobilisation if mechanism indicates
- Trauma team activation for major trauma
- Haemorrhage control
- Analgesia (IV for Orange/Red)

protocols.title: Allergic Reaction - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
ALLERGIC REACTION (Allergy, Anaphylaxis, Hives, Swelling)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise (stridor, tongue/throat swelling, unable to swallow)
- Inadequate breathing (severe wheeze, silent chest)
- Shock (hypotension, tachycardia, clammy)
- Unresponsive or responds to pain only
- Known anaphylaxis in progress

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- Stridor or respiratory distress with allergic symptoms
- Facial or lip swelling (angioedema)
- Spreading urticaria with systemic symptoms (dizziness, nausea)
- Previous anaphylaxis with current exposure to allergen
- Difficulty swallowing or speaking
- Wheeze with allergic reaction
- Abdominal symptoms with skin changes (anaphylaxis feature)
- Hypotension or near-syncope

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Widespread urticaria (hives) without systemic symptoms
- Localised angioedema (not face/airway)
- Moderate itch/discomfort
- Known allergy with new exposure (monitoring needed)
- Allergic reaction not responding to antihistamines
- Associated GI symptoms (vomiting, diarrhoea)

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Localised urticaria only
- Mild itching
- No systemic features
- Known mild allergic reaction, responding to treatment
- Contact dermatitis
- Insect bite with local reaction only

Key Discriminators:
- Airway swelling (face, tongue, throat)
- Breathing difficulty, Wheeze, Stridor
- Cardiovascular compromise
- Speed of onset, Previous anaphylaxis history

Immediate Actions:
- IM Adrenaline for anaphylaxis (0.5mg 1:1000)
- High flow oxygen
- IV access and fluids
- Antihistamines and steroids
- Continuous monitoring

protocols.title: Mental Health Crisis - Manchester Triage Protocol
protocols.text:
MENTAL HEALTH (Psychiatric emergency, Self-harm, Suicidal, Agitation)

RED - Immediate (Category 1):
- Airway compromise
- Inadequate breathing
- Shock
- Unresponsive (medical cause vs overdose)
- Currently actively harming self
- Currently actively harming others
- Medical emergency from overdose/self-harm

ORANGE - Very Urgent (Category 2):
- High risk of immediate self-harm or suicide
- Recent significant self-harm requiring treatment
- Significant overdose (actual or suspected)
- Severe agitation with risk to self or others
- Acute psychosis with disturbed behaviour
- Severe distress
- Needing physical restraint
- Command hallucinations to harm self/others
- Brought by police under Section 136

YELLOW - Urgent (Category 3):
- Moderate risk of self-harm
- Recent self-harm (wounds dressed, medically stable)
- Suicidal ideation without immediate plan
- Moderate agitation
- Acute anxiety/panic attack
- Known mental health crisis, worsening
- Alcohol/drug intoxication with psychiatric symptoms
- Distressed but able to engage

GREEN - Standard (Category 4):
- Low risk, seeking mental health support
- Chronic mental health symptoms, no acute change
- Anxiety symptoms, not in crisis
- Requests for mental health review
- Social crisis without psychiatric emergency
- Medication review/repeat prescription issues

Key Discriminators:
- Risk to self, Risk to others
- Active self-harm vs ideation
- Overdose/medical sequelae
- Level of agitation, Ability to engage
- Psychotic symptoms, Command hallucinations

Immediate Actions:
- Treat medical emergency first
- Safe environment (ligature-free, supervised)
- 1:1 observation for high risk
- De-escalation techniques
- Psychiatric liaison/crisis team referral
